title: A renamed module output
brief: Initialization works, but CI fails before you can review a deployment plan.
diagnostic:
Error: Unsupported attribute
  on outputs.tf line 3:
   3: value = module.service.internal_id
This object does not have an attribute named "internal_id".

options.label: Configuration validation
options.reason: The root asks for an output the child does not export. Check the child outputs first.

options.label: Provider API execution
options.reason: No remote API response appears in this diagnostic.

options.label: Backend locking
options.reason: No state-lock acquisition or owner is reported.

options.label: Increase the provider timeout
options.reason: A timeout cannot add an attribute to a module interface.

options.label: Compare the root reference with the child’s declared outputs
options.reason: Look at what the child exports, then use that output in the root.

options.label: Delete the provider lockfile
options.reason: Provider package selection does not define this child output.

questions.label: How would you check the fix?

options.label: Apply with -target and ignore the output
options.reason: Targeting another resource leaves the broken reference unresolved.

options.label: A formatter exits successfully
options.reason: Formatting can pass even when an output reference is wrong.

options.label: Correct the reference to the intended exported output, then validate and review a fresh plan
options.reason: Validate the corrected reference, then check a fresh plan with the original inputs.

title: Valid configuration, failing lint
brief: Validate passes locally, but CI rejects the same files in its pinned lint job.

options.label: Resource apply
options.reason: No resource operation failed.

options.label: Linting
options.reason: Validate and lint check different things. Read the named lint rule to see what it needs.

options.label: State migration
options.reason: No backend change or migration appears here.

options.label: Check the CI TFLint version/configuration and the variable declaration
options.reason: Run the failing rule locally and check which type the input should have.

options.label: Run terraform init -upgrade immediately
options.reason: Changing provider versions does not supply an explicit variable type.

options.label: Remove the lint step from CI
options.reason: That removes the evidence without resolving its cause.

questions.label: How would you check the fix?

options.label: A normal plan exits zero
options.reason: Without detailed exit codes, that neither proves no changes nor satisfies lint.

options.label: An unrelated resource name is changed
options.reason: It does not address the reported variable declaration.

options.label: Add the intended explicit type, rerun the pinned lint command, validate and inspect the plan
options.reason: Rerun the original rule and check that the configuration still behaves as intended.

title: Readonly initialization fails
brief: A branch changes the provider constraint, while the project still has its existing lockfile.
diagnostic:
Error: Inconsistent dependency lock file
Locked provider version 5.92.0 does not match the configured constraint ~> 6.0.0.
The dependency lock file is read-only.

options.label: Initialization and dependency selection
options.reason: The locked version does not match the allowed range, so init stops before planning.

options.label: Remote resource creation
options.reason: No cloud resource operation has started.

options.label: Input validation
options.reason: The error concerns a provider selection rather than a variable.

options.label: Hand-edit the provider checksum
options.reason: A checksum is integrity evidence, not an arbitrary setting to bypass.

options.label: Inspect the constraint/lockfile diff and decide whether the major upgrade was intentional
options.reason: Check whether the branch intended to change the provider version before editing the lockfile.

options.label: Remove all remote state
options.reason: State deletion cannot resolve incompatible package constraints.

questions.label: How would you check the fix?

options.label: Any downloaded provider binary is sufficient
options.reason: The source, allowed version and checksums must agree.

options.label: Keep rerunning readonly init unchanged
options.reason: The same incompatible inputs do not constitute a fix.

options.label: Restore the intended constraint or deliberately regenerate/review the lockfile, then readonly-init, validate and plan
options.reason: If the upgrade is intended, review compatibility and the plan too. Successful init is only the first check.

title: Instance keys are unknown
brief: The plan uses IDs from subnets that have not been created yet. Adding depends_on has not fixed the error.
diagnostic:
Error: Invalid for_each argument
The for_each set includes values derived from resource attributes that cannot be determined until apply.

options.label: Formatting
options.reason: Whitespace does not determine instance addresses.

options.label: Applying a saved plan
options.reason: There is no successful plan to apply yet.

options.label: Planning and expression evaluation
options.reason: Terraform needs those instance keys during planning, before the subnets exist.

options.label: Trace the collection’s keys and distinguish them from its values
options.reason: Use known names for the keys and keep the new IDs in the values.

options.label: Add more depends_on edges
options.reason: An ordering dependency does not make new resource IDs known during planning.

options.label: Set -refresh=false permanently
options.reason: Skipping refresh does not make an uncreated ID available.

questions.label: How would you check the fix?

options.label: A partial -target apply succeeds
options.reason: That can hide the graph problem and does not demonstrate a normal project plan.

options.label: Use stable known keys, then run a normal plan with the intended inputs and inspect the addresses
options.reason: Check that the resulting addresses use the stable names you intended.

options.label: The state file is empty
options.reason: Empty state cannot demonstrate that this expression can be planned.

title: AccessDenied after partial success
brief: Apply creates one resource, then hits an SSM permission error. Work out what succeeded before retrying.
diagnostic:
aws_s3_bucket.metadata: Creation complete
Error: AccessDeniedException: not authorized to perform ssm:PutParameter
  with aws_ssm_parameter.metadata

options.label: Provider API execution during apply
options.reason: One operation succeeded before the API denied the next one. Keep track of both.

options.label: Provider checksum verification
options.reason: The provider has already executed API operations.

options.label: Source formatting
options.reason: No formatting diagnostic explains an authorization denial.

options.label: Delete state and begin again
options.reason: That can orphan the bucket that was already created.

options.label: Increase every timeout
options.reason: A permanent permission denial is not repaired by waiting longer.

options.label: Check the effective provider role/action/resource/region and inspect the partial state/live IDs
options.reason: Check who is running, which permission is missing and which resource already exists.

questions.label: How would you check the fix?

options.label: The CLI can authenticate under some profile
options.reason: That does not prove the provider’s effective role has the required permission.

options.label: Correct the scoped cause, generate a fresh reviewed plan, and verify the resumed result and cleanup
options.reason: A fresh plan includes what already succeeded, so you can review the remaining work.

options.label: Hide the failed resource with -target
options.reason: That leaves the project’s intended operation unresolved.

title: A lock belongs to a running job
brief: You cannot plan because a CI apply still owns the state lock.
diagnostic:
Error acquiring the state lock
Operation: OperationTypeApply
Who: ci-deploy-42
Path: environment/dev/terraform.tfstate

options.label: Variable type checking
options.reason: The error concerns concurrent state access.

options.label: Backend/state coordination
options.reason: The lock tells you which run currently owns state access.

options.label: Module installation
options.reason: No module download is being diagnosed.

options.label: Force-unlock immediately
options.reason: An active owner still needs protection against concurrent writers.

options.label: Disable locking for this run
options.reason: That bypasses the concurrency protection while another writer is active.

options.label: Confirm the exact backend/workspace and inspect the owning CI run
options.reason: Find the owning run first; it may still need the lock.

questions.label: How would you check the fix?

options.label: Let the owner finish or cancel through its normal workflow, confirm release, then run a fresh plan
options.reason: Consider force-unlock only after confirming the exact lock is stale.

options.label: Manually remove the lock while the owner runs
options.reason: Its continued operation could still write state concurrently.

options.label: Delete the workload’s state object
options.reason: That destroys tracking rather than resolving legitimate ownership.

title: A repair proposes replacement
brief: A small variable-file change now plans a replacement. Find out why before applying it.

options.label: Provider installation
options.reason: The provider is already able to compute a resource change.

options.label: A failed formatting check
options.reason: A diff in infrastructure arguments is not a formatting diagnostic.

options.label: Planning and change review
options.reason: The plan is asking to replace a resource. Find the reason before approving it.

options.label: Assume every replacement is corrupt state
options.reason: A changed immutable argument can legitimately require replacement.

options.label: Compare the selected variable files, source diff and provider replacement cause
options.reason: Check whether the CIDR change was intended or the wrong inputs were selected.

options.label: Use state rm to silence the diff
options.reason: The old subnet remains live and the next plan can propose another object.

questions.label: How would you check the fix?

options.label: Use a moved block to ignore an actual CIDR change
options.reason: Address refactoring does not override an immutable-argument change.

options.label: Apply the surprising plan without review
options.reason: Success would not establish that the intended environment was selected.

options.label: Correct accidental inputs or review the intentional replacement, then verify a fresh plan in the same environment
options.reason: Rerun the plan with the intended inputs and check that the proposed actions are right.
